etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English contradiccioun, contradiction, from Old French contradiction, from Latin contrādictiō, from contrādīcō (“speak against”).

definitions.definition: (countable) A statement that contradicts itself, i.e., a statement that claims that the same thing is true and that it is false at the same time and in the same senses of the terms.

There is a contradiction in what you sa: she can't be both married and single.

definitions.definition: (countable) A logical inconsistency among two or more elements or propositions.
(logic, countable) A proposition that is false for all values of its propositional variables or Boolean atoms.
